Reproducing a published bicycle-frame surrogate benchmark, then extending it with physics

Alfred ChettiarLinkedInGitHub repository 2026-11-26

A peer-reviewed dataset of 4,047 FE-simulated tubular frames, the paper's claims re-derived from its released data, its surrogate benchmark rebuilt, and this project's physics-informed models measured against it on identical folds.

Summary

  • 11 of 11 checkable dataset claims in the paper reproduce from the released data within tolerance (frame counts, the non-dominated set and the three case-study frames).
  • Rebuilt with the authors' own hyperparameters, the paper's models keep their published ranking; on the released data they score higher than published (best reproduced R² 0.737 vs 0.605 published).
  • Adding this project's beam-theory features and log-scaled targets lifts the best model to R² 0.747 (AutoGluon + physics): +0.010 R² and -13 % MAE against the best reproduced paper model, AutoML (AutoGluon), on identical folds (R² gain not significant over 5 folds, p = 0.15).
  • The best single model, a deep ensemble + physics, reaches R² 0.734, on par with the AutoML ensemble, and adds 95 % intervals (conservative: they cover 94.6–98.4 % of held-out frames) that the paper's models do not provide.
  • Re-sizing the tubes of the paper's titanium road frame (frame 3853) gives a design at -23.8 % mass (against the surrogate's own 2.55 kg prediction for the reference; FE: 2.84 kg) with -30.5 % in-plane deflection and mean SF ≥ 1. Demanding SF ≥ 1 on the 95 % lower bound instead costs mass (see Optimisation). Surrogate predictions only, not FE re-verified.

Source

The reference is FRAMED [1], a peer-reviewed study from the MIT DeCoDE Lab published in Computer-Aided Design (Elsevier, 2023), with its dataset and code released under the MIT licence [2]. It holds 4,047 community-designed bicycle frames (39 inputs: 18 geometry relations, 9 tube outer diameters, 7 wall thicknesses, 2 bridge flags, 3 materials), each solved in SolidWorks under three load cases: in-plane (2,000 N), transverse (500 N) and eccentric (2,000 N + 140 N·m). Ten outputs are recorded: seven deflections and rotations, two safety factors and the mass. A bicycle's rear triangle is a tubular two-wheeler rear sub-frame, the same class of structure as this project's original V1 study.

The authors checked their FE setup with a mesh-convergence study and against physical frame tests (their Table 3, repeated below from the paper; it is not something this project re-ran).

Table 4 reproduction

The paper's five regressors were rebuilt with the best hyperparameters the authors report (their Tables 6–9) and scored on 10 × 5-fold cross-validation, with inputs and outputs standardised inside each training fold. R² and MAE are averaged over the ten standardised outputs, as in the paper. A model passes when both are within ±0.05 of Table 4. AutoML (AutoGluon) runs on 1 × 5 folds to bound its run time.

The paper's ranking (AutoML (AutoGluon) > XGBoost > Neural network > Decision tree > K-nearest neighbours) is preserved.

Every reproduced model scores higher than published, by 0.05–0.13 R²; MAE lands close to the paper's (within 0.046). The paper's MSE values (≈1.0) cannot come from unit-variance targets at its own R². The likeliest cause is data version: the paper trained on 4,118 frames, the public release holds 4,047, so 71 frames, plausibly the most extreme, are missing. The authors' AutoML training code is not public, so the protocol above is inferred. These gaps are reported, not tuned away.

Improvements

This project's surrogates add what the paper's models lack: beam-theory features computed from each tube (area, bending and torsional stiffness EI and GJ, slenderness, an analytic mass estimate ρ·A·L, yield strength), log-scaled targets for the heavy-tailed deflections, physical guardrails on every prediction, and uncertainty intervals. All models below share the paper models' exact folds, so every comparison is paired.

Optimisation

The paper names constrained optimisation with its surrogates as future work. Here the paper's case-study titanium road frame (frame 3853, 2.84 kg) keeps its rider-fit geometry, and NSGA-II varies the outer diameter and wall thickness of the top, down and seat tubes and the stays (10 variables, within the dataset's 1st–99th percentile). Objectives: minimum mass and minimum in-plane dropout deflection. Constraints: both safety factors ≥ 1, transverse deflection no worse than the reference, D/t ≤ 50. Each material is run twice: nominal uses the mean prediction of the deep ensemble + physics, robust requires SF ≥ 1 on its lower 95 % bound. The gap between the two is the mass price of certainty.

In FE the reference frame has SF 1.29 / 1.07 and 2.84 kg. The surrogate's safety-factor intervals are wide (the paper warns its SF labels are mesh-sensitive). The surrogate predicts the reference itself at 2.55 kg and SF 1.10 / 0.90, so both runs treat it as infeasible, and all changes below are relative to that prediction. All designs are surrogate predictions; none was re-checked in FE. "Nearest design" is the standardised distance to the closest simulated frame; for comparison, a typical FRAMED frame sits 2.88 from its nearest neighbour.

Limitations

  • The structure is a bicycle frame, not a motorcycle sub-frame. It is the closest public, peer-reviewed, tube-parametric two-wheeler dataset available.
  • The paper's AutoML protocol is inferred; its code is not public. The released data hold 4,047 frames vs 4,118 in the paper, and the paper's MSE values are inconsistent with its R².
  • Safety factors come from SolidWorks solid meshes; the authors note they include stress singularities at tube junctions (paper Sec. 3.5), so SF labels are noisier than deflections.
  • Optimised designs are surrogate predictions without FE re-verification (FE was out of scope).
  • Repeated cross-validation folds overlap; significance uses the corrected resampled t-test, but p-values remain approximate.
  • The analytic mass estimate leaves out the top tube and seat stays, which have no length parameter.

Method & hardware

Data: all_structural_data_oh.csv from [2] at commit b881634, verified by SHA-256. Outputs follow the authors' notebook (absolute values of deflections). Folds: 10 repeats × 5-fold KFold, seed 42. Reproduce everything with python -m src.framed.run --stage all.
